A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Dream4Drive and DriveObj3D. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison despite reformatting and appendix expansion.

before.justification: v3 reports original nuScenes detection, tracking, insertion ablation, controllability and generation-quality results in Section 5 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds asset-quality measurements, synthesis-cost estimates, scaling experiments, style-transfer evaluations and selection-sensitivity studies.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendix A.1 retain the same guidance maps, FusionNet/DiT architecture, losses and asset-generation pipeline. The expanded sample-construction description clarifies existing operations; the additional style-transfer experiment does not specify a revision to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: The nuScenes domain, object categories and detection/tracking tasks remain unchanged. v4 adds explicitly evaluated rain/night synthetic conditions through style-transfer augmentation (Table 9 and Figures 19–22), extending environmental coverage within the existing domain.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in the matched detection, tracking, asset-source and generation-quality comparisons. The new asset-similarity evaluation reuses Trellis and Hunyuan3D, already compared in v3; newly cited works are not additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v4 adds asset evaluation using CLIP/DINO image similarity and controlled experiments with 7/14/35 scenes, 420 versus 840 synthetic samples, 2/5/8 m/s trajectories and alternative asset/scene selections. These substantially expand evaluation design. The original splits, epoch/resolution comparisons and generator-training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v3's position, distance, asset-source and guidance-map ablations, v4 tests synthetic-data scaling, environmental diversification, trajectory speed and sensitivity to selected assets and scenes (Table 5 and Tables 8–11). These address previously untested questions about augmentation limits and selection dependence.

E5.justification: Appendix A.4 newly reports separate outcomes for three random asset groups and three scene selections, providing limited replication and variability information about data selection. Neither version reports training-seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: The original main and matched appendix scores remain unchanged, but substantial new results are reported. At 1× training, Table 8 gives mAP 40.7/40.4/39.7 for 7/14/35 scenes; Table 9 reports 41.2 with 420 additional style-transferred samples versus 40.7 with the original 420. New tables also report asset-similarity advantages and selection robustness, while Table 5 adds speed-dependent results.

T1.justification: The diffusion, conditioning, fusion and loss equations, including Appendix A.1's masked-MSE and LPIPS formulations, are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, theoretical results, proofs or substantive derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims: prior comparisons confound training epochs, Dream4Drive improves perception with fewer than 2% additional samples, and DriveObj3D supports diverse asset insertion. The additional experiments support and qualify these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendices A.3–A.4 add substantive interpretations: excessive OOD data may dilute in-distribution signal, environmental/layout diversity matters more than volume, faster trajectories help distant-object learning, and asset/scene selection has limited influence in the tested settings. These materially extend the applicability discussion. Appendix E's collision/drivability limitation is retained.

D1.justification: v3 briefly describes 420 category-balanced samples; v4 explains their construction from seven scenes, ten categories and six keyframes. It adds MLLM-assisted selection and its full prompt, human verification, pyrender orientation calibration, inference-step details, and automated/manual costs of 9800/295 seconds. Metric model identifiers and a code-release commitment are also added; release availability is not established.

R1.justification: The citation set is revised, including additions such as CLIP, DINOv2, SimGen and WorldSplat and removal of several multimodal-language references. The related-work discussion retains its central positioning around geometric control, realistic editing and fair downstream comparisons.

P1.justification: v4 compresses part of the introduction, adds explanatory transitions, expands Appendix A into synthesis and experimental subsections, and adds acknowledgments, ethics and reproducibility statements. Author affiliations and headings change, but most existing prose and the main narrative order are retained.

P2.justification: v4 adopts conference formatting throughout, replaces the branded title-page design, moves Figure 1 above the abstract, and resizes/repositions many displays. It expands Table 5, adds Tables 6–11 and Figures 19–22, and places the retained Figures 17–18 together. Earlier appendix displays are retained under changed numbering and placement.

improvement.justification: The added selection-sensitivity and scaling experiments strengthen assessment of the central 420-sample result, including useful evidence that more synthetic scenes can hurt performance. Appendix A.2 and Listing 1 improve construction and cost transparency. These are meaningful incremental gains, although the new studies still lack formal uncertainty estimates and leave the MLLM identity and style-transfer implementation underspecified.
